issues.body:
The [Nemotron post-training v3 collection](https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/nemotron-post-training-v3) contains 16 `Nemotron-SFT-*` datasets that are absent from `all_sources()`. Register them as materializable Datakit sources so mixtures can select their advertised configs and splits independently.

Sources:

- [nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Agentic-v2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Agentic-v2)
- [nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-OpenCode-v1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-OpenCode-v1)
- [nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-SWE-v2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-SWE-v2)
- [nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Safety-v1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Safety-v1)
- [nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Competitive-Programming-v2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Competitive-Programming-v2)
- [nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Instruction-Following-Chat-v2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Instruction-Following-Chat-v2)
- [nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Multilingual-v1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Multilingual-v1)
- [nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-ARC-AGI-v1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-ARC-AGI-v1)

- [nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Instruction-Following-Chat-v3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Instruction-Following-Chat-v3)
- [nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Math-v4](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Math-v4)
- [nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Multilingual-v2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Multilingual-v2)
- [nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Safety-v2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Safety-v2)

The repositories contain about 16.6 million records and 556 GB of raw files. This is not a unique-record count because dataset versions and ARC-AGI blends overlap. Most sources are JSONL; SWE-v3 is Parquet. Nine repositories currently fail Hugging Face dataset-server conversion, and one ARC-AGI config fails, so ingestion must use pinned repository files instead of depending on the generated viewer. Agentic and ARC-AGI records include structured messages, reasoning, tool definitions, calls, and outputs that need deterministic serialization.

Done when:

- All 16 Hugging Face repositories use immutable revisions and appear in `lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/sources.py`.
- Advertised configs and splits with distinct mixture semantics have separate source keys.
- Normalization emits canonical text documents while retaining dataset and split identity. Structured agent records retain roles, reasoning, tool definitions, calls, and outputs in the serialized text.
- One-time tokenizer jobs provide the token counts recorded in `sources.py`.
- Tests cover source discovery and structured agent-record serialization.
- The sources materialize without schema errors through the Datakit ferry on GCP and CoreWeave.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue and confirm actionability
- [x] Research datakit source registry + download-module patterns
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight
- [x] Post Research + proposed approach for human review

No PR: this is a multi-module feature that needs one-time cluster tokenizer jobs and a cross-cloud ferry run, neither of which an autonomous PR can perform or verify. Analysis for a human below.

# Research

The issue targets the **post-training v3** collection (16 standalone `nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-*` repos), which is different in kind from what the registry already carries. The registered `nemotron_sft/*` keys come from the single `nvidia/Nemotron-Pretraining-SFT-v1` repo and are **plain-text parquet** normalized with a bare `text_field` — no transform. The v3 repos are **structured SFT records** (messages, reasoning, tool definitions/calls/outputs) and are **mostly JSONL, with SWE-v3 in Parquet**, so the bare-`text_field` path in `nemotron_v2.py` does not apply. They need a `row_to_doc` serialization transform before `normalize_step`, like `nemotron_terminal.py`.

Two facts make this not autonomously completable end-to-end: the registry requires a **measured token count per source** (one-time tokenizer job over the normalized artifact — see the exact-count comments in `sources.py`), and "Done when" requires the sources to **materialize through the ferry on GCP and CoreWeave**. Both are cluster operations.

**Relevant code**
- [`sources.py#L367`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/sources.py#L367) — existing `nemotron_sft/*` rows (pretraining v1, plain-text parquet — not v3)
- [`nemotron_terminal.py#L25`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/nemotron_terminal.py#L25) — `row_to_doc` + transform + `(processed, normalize)` chain to copy
- [`rollout_transforms.py#L51`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/rollout_transforms.py#L51) — `render_role_message` / `render_tool_message` / `render_tool_call` / `text_document`; reuse for structured serialization
- [`nemotron_v2.py#L193`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/nemotron_v2.py#L193) — cached family download + per-subset normalize + `{marin_name: (download, normalize)}` factory
- [`huggingface.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/huggingface.py) — `download_hf_step` pins a revision and fetches raw repo files (covers the 9 repos whose dataset-server conversion fails)

# Proposed approach (design change)

**1. One download module, 16 repos.** Add `lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/nemotron_sft_v3.py`. These are 16 *separate* repos (not one repo with subset globs), so model it as a dataclass table keyed by marin_name: each row = `(hf_dataset_id, immutable_revision, format, split/config selectors)`. Each repo gets its own `download_hf_step` with a pinned revision — no shared family download, unlike v2. Do **not** depend on the generated viewer; `download_hf_step` already fetches pinned files, covering the 9 conversion failures and the ARC-AGI config failure.

**2. Serialization (`row_to_doc`).** Two shapes:
- *Plain SFT* (math, science, safety, multilingual, etc.): render the messages list with `render_role_message`, join, wrap in `text_document`.
- *Structured agent* (Agentic-v2, ARC-AGI-v1): use `render_tool_message`/`render_tool_call` so roles, reasoning, tool definitions, calls, and outputs survive into the text. Tool *definitions* aren't rendered by the current helpers — add a small `render_tool_definitions` helper in `rollout_transforms.py` (shared, not per-repo). Emit canonical text while keeping dataset + split identity in the `source` field.
- Reader: Parquet via `load_parquet_batched` (SWE-v3); JSONL via a `Dataset.from_files("**/*.jsonl")` reader (precedent in `superior_reasoning.py` / `gpt_oss_rollouts.py`).

**3. Separate source keys per advertised config/split** with distinct mixture semantics (ARC-AGI blends, versioned Math v3/v4, Multilingual v1/v2, Instruction-Following v2/v3, Safety v1/v2, SWE v2/v3). Where a repo advertises multiple configs/splits that mix differently, give each its own `nemotron_sft_v3/<repo>/<config>` key; collapse to one key only when splits share semantics.

**4. Registry wiring.** Add a `nemotron_sft_v3` group in `all_sources()` from the module's `{marin_name: (download, normalize)}` factory, spliced into `all_rows`.

**5. Token counts.** Land the code with **placeholder counts marked TODO** (as `nemotron_code_v1/content` already does), then run the one-time tokenizer jobs and replace with measured `tokens/docs` figures in a follow-up — matching every exact-count comment in `sources.py`. This is the required cluster step.

**6. Tests** (`tests/datakit/download/test_nemotron_sft_v3.py`): (a) source discovery — every advertised key appears in `all_sources()` with pinned revisions and no duplicate marin_name; (b) structured-record serialization — feed a fixture Agentic/ARC-AGI row through `row_to_doc` and assert roles, reasoning, tool definitions, calls, and outputs all appear in the emitted text. No mocks; behavior-focused.

**Sequencing for a human:** (1) module + serialization + registry (placeholder counts) + tests → reviewable PR; (2) tokenizer jobs → measured counts; (3) ferry materialization on GCP + CoreWeave to close "Done when". Steps 2–3 need cluster access.

Open question for the owner: should the 16 v3 SFT repos live under a new `nemotron_sft_v3/*` namespace (recommended — keeps them distinct from the pretraining-v1 `nemotron_sft/*` already registered), or fold into the existing `nemotron_sft/*` prefix?

issues.author: ravwojdyla-agent
issues.body:
Echo gives agents search across the wiki, repository files, pull requests, issues, and Discord. We do not know whether Echo makes agent sessions better or worse. `infra/echo/search_benchmark.py` scores retrieval relevance against graded judgments, but it does not measure the effect on the session that made the query.

Build an analysis that runs on a developer machine and reads local agent session transcripts. Central collection of sessions is not necessary. Claude Code writes JSONL transcripts to `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/`. The transcripts record Echo calls as Bash tool calls to `infra/echo/cli.py`.

For each Echo call, an agent-based classifier gives one outcome:
- Helpful: the agent used a fact from the result, changed the plan, or did not do the same work again
- Neutral: the agent read the result and did not use it
- Harmful: the result was wrong or not current and the agent acted on it, or the search used turns and gave nothing

Report rates for each outcome, divided by Echo domain (wiki, files, pull requests, issues, discord) and by command (`search` or `get`). Keep the worst examples so that a person can review the classifier.

Done when:
- A script in `infra/echo/` reads local transcripts and emits one record for each Echo call
- The classifier gives helpful, neutral, or harmful with a short reason and the transcript turns that support it
- The script prints rates by domain and by command, and writes the records to a file
- A person reviews a sample of the labels, and the agreement rate is in the output
- The analysis runs on one machine, and it adds no central data collection

issues.author: Helw150
issues.body:
Instruction backtranslation over Stack v3 repositories that use scientific software: the repository is the response, and GLM-5.2 writes the brief a scientist would hand a language model to build it from scratch, making explicit what the code leaves implicit (the scientific question, why each tool fits, the parameters that encode domain judgement, expected outputs).

Detection and prompt extraction exist but are uncommitted: `experiments/datakit/scientific_software.py`, `experiments/datakit/repo_backtranslation.py`, and two scripts under `experiments/datakit/scripts/`. They call a `raw_stack_v3_step()` extraction in `lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/stack_v3.py` that was reverted out of #7788 and has to land with them.

Detection covers 44 tools across materials and chemistry, bioinformatics, imaging, and workflow engines. It keys on structured signals — Python imports, R `library()`, dependency manifests, command invocations in shell/Nextflow/Snakemake, bioconda channel references, and signature filenames such as `INCAR`/`POSCAR` — because most of the tool names are ordinary English words and substring matching is useless on them. Over the full corpus 146,661 of 172,898,790 repositories match, of which 9,089 have at least 10 stars. Prompt corpus at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/analysis/stack-v3-backtranslation-prompts_4141dfc2` and scan manifest at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/analysis/stack-v3-scientific-software_686e7bbe`; both were written by the current rules, and neither row count has been verified since the last rules change.

GLM-5.2-FP8 serving is not built. It needs 8 GB200s across two nodes with Ray and tensor parallel 8, which does not fit the single-Iris-task constraint in `lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py:330`, so it means porting the hand-rolled serve from `experiments/kernelgym/collect_glm52_rollouts.py`.

Repository selection is unresolved. 2,670 of the 9,089 match a single tool through a single evidence file, the profile of an incidental hit: `github-linguist/linguist` matches 11 tools from `samples/`, `XAMPPRocky/tokei` matches 5 from `tests/data/`. A test-path blacklist would be wrong, since `google-deepmind/alphafold`'s evidence includes `relax/utils_test.py`. Requiring corroboration — two evidence kinds, or import/dependency evidence rather than a lone command match — is the likelier lever.

Done when:
- Detection and prompt extraction are committed with tests, including the `raw_stack_v3_step()` extraction they depend on.
- The prompt corpus row count is verified against the starred population.
- A repository-selection rule is chosen and applied.
- GLM-5.2 has generated briefs for the selected repositories into a Parquet artifact carrying repo_path, matched tools, and token counts per row.

comments.body:

# Assessment

Large multi-module feature, not a self-contained fix — new detection + prompt-extraction modules, a reverted `raw_stack_v3_step()` extraction, custom multi-node GLM-5.2-FP8 serving, plus corpus verification and generation. Well over the PR threshold, so this is analysis for human review rather than a PR.

**Blocker: the source this depends on is not in the repo.** Every file the issue names as "uncommitted" is absent from the checkout, and no branch carries them:

- `experiments/datakit/scientific_software.py` — missing
- `experiments/datakit/repo_backtranslation.py` — missing
- two scripts under `experiments/datakit/scripts/` — not present (dir holds `generate_tier2_skewed.py`, `sync_datakit.py`, `trigger_sources.py`, `upload_tier2_skewed_to_hf.py`, `validate_ferry_outputs.py`)
- `raw_stack_v3_step()` in [`stack_v3.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/stack_v3.py) — absent (only `processed_stack_v3_step()` exists); it was reverted out of #7788 as the issue notes
- `experiments/kernelgym/collect_glm52_rollouts.py` — missing (nearest is [`glm_kernelgym_rollouts.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/glm_kernelgym_rollouts.py), a dataset transform, not a serve)

An agent can't land uncommitted work it doesn't have. **Please push your local branch** (detection, prompt extraction, `raw_stack_v3_step()`, the two scripts) so the committing + testing + selection-rule work has a base to build on.

**Relevant code**
- [`stack_v3.py#L171-L205`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/stack_v3.py#L171-L205) — where `raw_stack_v3_step()` must re-land, alongside `processed_stack_v3_step()`
- [`inference/iris.py#L329-L336`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py#L329-L336) — `remote_inference` runs inside one Iris job; TP8 across 8 GB200s / two nodes with Ray doesn't fit this, hence the hand-rolled serve
- [`glm_kernelgym_rollouts.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/glm_kernelgym_rollouts.py) — existing GLM-5.2 dataset transform; the serve referenced (`collect_glm52_rollouts.py`) is not committed

# Proposed approach (for review before implementation)

Split the "Done when" list into reviewable PRs rather than one drop:

1. **Land the extraction + detection first.** Push the local branch; re-add `raw_stack_v3_step()` to `stack_v3.py` with a test, then `scientific_software.py` detection (imports, `library()`, manifests, shell/Nextflow/Snakemake invocations, bioconda channels, signature filenames like `INCAR`/`POSCAR`) with fixture-repo tests over a handful of true/false positives. This is the natural first PR.
2. **Repository-selection rule.** The incidental-hit profile (2,670/9,089 = single tool via single evidence file; `linguist` 11 tools from `samples/`, `tokei` 5 from `tests/data/`) argues for requiring corroboration — two evidence kinds, or import/dependency evidence over a lone command match — not a test-path blacklist (which would drop `alphafold`, whose evidence includes `relax/utils_test.py`). Encode the rule in detection, unit-test it against those named repos, then re-scan and record the new starred count.
3. **Corpus row-count verification.** The prompt corpus (`stack-v3-backtranslation-prompts_4141dfc2`) and scan manifest (`stack-v3-scientific-software_686e7bbe`) predate the last rules change; both need re-derivation and a verified count against the ≥10-star population (9,089) after the selection rule lands. Depends on 1–2.
4. **GLM-5.2-FP8 serving.** Porting a multi-node Ray + TP8 serve is its own PR and the largest risk. It belongs after the corpus is settled and should link a short design note (where the serve lives, how it's launched outside `remote_inference`'s single-task model, and how briefs get written to Parquet with `repo_path`, matched tools, and per-row token counts).

Sequencing 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 keeps each PR reviewable and lets the selection rule (which changes counts) settle before regenerating corpora. Happy to take PR 1 once the branch is pushed.

issues.author: rjpower
issues.body:
Marin has several operational metric paths, but coverage and identity differ by subsystem. Levanter and native vLLM publish Prometheus-compatible metrics through Telltale. Iris writes task, worker, state, event, and provisioning rows. Zephyr writes stage and shard rows directly. SkyRL and several evaluation and service paths have no equivalent producer.

The rows cannot always be joined. Zephyr stats omit Iris job, task, attempt, and worker identity. Kubernetes task rows name the pod but not its node, so they cannot be joined to node-level DCGM readings. The accelerator fields on `iris.task` are not populated. Arbitrary Iris tasks do not start durable Telltale forwarding by default.

In scope: Iris control-plane and workload metrics, Levanter training, native vLLM and evaluation serving, Zephyr pipelines, and Marin RL/SkyRL. Model-quality metrics remain in W&B and evaluation records remain in Evaldash. Logs, traces, profiles, and Finelog deployment work are separate branches of #5198.

Done when:

- A checked-in producer matrix lists each in-scope process, its metric families, identity fields, cadence, Finelog namespace, and Grafana or alert consumer.
- Workload rows carry an unambiguous cluster, root job, task, attempt, worker or node, process or rank, and role where those fields apply. Service rows carry cluster, component, instance, and version identity.
- Metric names, units, types, reset behavior, cadence, and label-cardinality limits are documented and tested.
- Every in-scope workload reports readiness or phase, progress or completed work, failures or retries, latency, and saturation when the signal exists.
- Zephyr metrics can be filtered to one execution and joined to its Iris job.
- Iris task metrics can be joined to node-level GPU telemetry, and the existing accelerator fields are populated or removed in favor of the canonical source.
- A bounded smoke for each producer queries its rows from Finelog after the process exits and verifies the expected identity and metric families without parsing logs.
- #7795 can build one run view from these identities, and #6598 can aggregate resource usage without subsystem-specific name parsing.

Part of #5198. #7798 is the first producer-specific child.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body: 🤖 This issue is the operational metrics contract branch of #5198. #7798 covers SkyRL worker telemetry, and #7681 covers Levanter rank-level straggler reporting. #7795 and #6598 are the first consumers of the shared identities.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Analysis — not opening a PR.** This is a cross-subsystem epic (a producer matrix plus identity/schema work across Iris, Levanter, vLLM, Zephyr, and SkyRL, with 8 acceptance bullets). Well past the ~100-line self-contained bug bar, so posting root-cause + a proposed decomposition for a human to review before implementation.

# Research

The forwarding path already exists and stamps full Iris identity; the gaps are (a) directly-written stat rows that omit that identity and (b) unpopulated/unjoinable fields.

- Telltale metrics already carry `job_id, task_index, attempt, worker, region, process_index`, stamped authoritatively at scrape time and written to the `telltale` namespace — so Levanter/vLLM rows are already joinable to Iris. [`rigging/telltale.py#L186-L231`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/rigging/src/rigging/telltale.py#L186-L231), [`iris/runtime/telltale.py#L31-L62`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/runtime/telltale.py#L31-L62)
- `iris.task` rows have `task_id, attempt_id, worker_id` but **no `root_job_id`**, and `accelerator_util_pct`/`accelerator_mem_bytes` are nullable and (per issue) unpopulated. No node id, so no join to node-level DCGM. [`iris/cluster/stats/tables.py#L146-L166`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/stats/tables.py#L146-L166)
- `zephyr.stage`/`zephyr.worker` rows carry only `execution_id` — no Iris `job/task/attempt/worker`, so they cannot be filtered to one execution's Iris job. [`zephyr/stats.py#L71-L115`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/stats.py#L71-L115)
- Pod name is captured (`TaskStatus.container_id`) and `attempt_uid` reaches `TaskEventRow`, but neither pod name nor node reaches `iris.task`. [`job.proto#L215`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/rpc/job.proto#L215), [`reconcile/commit.py#L253-L273`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/commit.py#L253-L273)
- SkyRL has no Finelog producer — tracked separately as the first producer child #7798.
- Prior design context: [`.agents/projects/2026-07-24_grafana_unified_jobs_and_finelog_federation.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/.agents/projects/2026-07-24_grafana_unified_jobs_and_finelog_federation.md) (cluster stamping, `iris.task_state` emission), and the alert contract joining telltale to `iris.task_state` via `(cluster, root_job_id)` in [`docs/ops/training-stall-alert-contract.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/docs/ops/training-stall-alert-contract.md).

# Proposed decomposition

The epic mixes documentation (producer matrix), schema changes (Iris/Zephyr identity), and per-producer smokes. It should land as separate PRs, each independently reviewable and testable. Suggested children under this issue:

1. **Producer matrix doc** — checked-in table: each in-scope process → metric families, identity fields, cadence, Finelog namespace, Grafana/alert consumer. Pure docs; establishes the contract the schema PRs implement against.
2. **Iris `iris.task` identity + accelerator fields** — add `root_job_id` (derivable from the `task_id` path via `Namespace.from_job_id`), add `pod_name`/`node`, and either populate the accelerator fields from the worker usage sample or remove them in favor of the canonical DCGM/node source. Enables the `iris.task` ↔ node-DCGM join. Test: emit a task attempt, query the row from Finelog, assert `root_job_id` and node/pod are non-null.
3. **Zephyr → Iris linkage** — thread `job_id/task_id/attempt_id/worker_id` (available in the runner's Iris job context) onto `zephyr.stage` and `zephyr.worker`. Test: run a small pipeline under Iris, assert both namespaces filter to one execution and join to its `iris.task`.
4. **Per-producer durability smokes** — one bounded smoke per producer that queries its rows from Finelog *after the process exits* and asserts identity + expected metric families, no log parsing. Reuses the pattern the telltale forwarder already implies.
5. **Metric-name/label registry** — document and test names, units, types, reset behavior, cadence, and label-cardinality limits (guards SkyRL/#7798 and future producers).

Ordering: (1) first to fix the contract, then (2)/(3) in parallel, then (4)/(5). Each is <200 LOC and independently mergeable.

Open questions for a human before implementation:
- Populate the accelerator fields on `iris.task` from the worker heartbeat (`IrisWorkerStat.gpu_util_pct`/`hbm_used_bytes` already exist per worker), or **remove** them and always read from node-level DCGM? The issue lists both as acceptable — pick one.
- Node identity for the DCGM join: add `node` to `iris.task` (worker-emitted), or join `iris.task.worker_id` → `iris.worker` → node? The latter avoids schema churn if `iris.worker` can carry node.

Happy to take child #1 (producer matrix) or #2 (Iris identity) as the first concrete PR once the two questions above are settled.

issues.author: weaverbot
issues.body:
The shared evaluation launcher accepts a model and eval subset, but every run is still started manually. #6503 requires an eligible checkpoint to trigger its configured evaluations and publish results without an operator invoking the CLI.

Done when:

- A checkpoint has an explicit, reviewable evaluation policy: eligibility, model configuration, eval subset, and retry behavior.
- An idempotent trigger launches the existing evaluation pipeline when an eligible checkpoint becomes available.
- Repeated events do not create duplicate runs for the same checkpoint, evaluation, and version.
- Trigger state and terminal run records are inspectable, and failures can be retried without editing database state by hand.
- A canary demonstrates checkpoint availability through indexed evaldash results with no manual launch step.

Part of #6503.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read AGENTS.md, fix-issue, commit skills
- [x] Actionability check (clear "Done when" → actionable)
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (no open PR/issue)
- [x] Research existing eval infra
- [x] Post Research + proposed approach
- [ ] Awaiting human review before implementation (scope > PR threshold)

# Research

Scope is a new event-driven subsystem (trigger + policy + idempotent state + retry + canary), not a self-contained bug fix, so this is an analysis for review rather than a PR. The pieces to build on already exist:

- **Launcher** `experiments/evaluation/launch.py:98-154` — `build_evaluation_batch()` / `launch_group()` take a model + eval keys and submit one Iris orchestrator. This is the "existing evaluation pipeline" the trigger must call.
- **Record store** `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/records.py:114-159` — `EvalRunRecord` is the source of truth; `record_path()` is `{prefix}/{run_id}/record.json`. evaldash indexes these.
- **evaldash ingest** `infra/evaldash/src/server.py:289-370` — poll-based ingest (300s) of terminal records into Postgres; this is where the canary must show results with no manual launch.
- **Checkpoint discovery** `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/utils.py:9-21` (`discover_hf_checkpoints`) and `experiments/grug/checkpointing.py:40-76` (`metadata.json` → `step`, `timestamp`) — on-demand only; nothing watches for readiness.

**Idempotency blocker:** `launch.py:72-74` `_run_id()` = timestamp + `uuid4()`, so it is non-deterministic. Replaying the same checkpoint event today produces a *new* `run_id` and a duplicate run. The DoD "repeated events do not create duplicate runs for the same checkpoint, evaluation, and version" therefore requires a deterministic idempotency key; it cannot be met by reusing `_run_id` as-is.

Nothing exists for: checkpoint eligibility policy, an event/trigger, trigger state, or checkpoint→run linkage.

# Proposed approach (for review)

Smallest design that satisfies each DoD bullet. Reuse the launcher unchanged except for the run-id path.

**1. Eligibility + policy (reviewable config).** A dataclass `CheckpointEvalPolicy` in `experiments/evaluation/` declaring: eligibility predicate (`step % N == 0`, or min-step, or an explicit allowlist), `model` config template, `evals` subset (reuse `EVALS`/`SUITES` keys), and `max_retries`. Policies live in-repo next to `models.py`/`evals.py` so they diff in PRs. No per-checkpoint DB config.

**2. Deterministic run id → idempotency.** Add `eval_run_id(checkpoint_id, eval_key, version)` returning a stable hash-suffixed id (drop the timestamp+uuid for triggered runs). Idempotency then falls out of the existing object layout: a run exists iff `record.json` is present at its deterministic `record_path`. The trigger skips any eval whose record already exists in a terminal-success state; retry re-launches only records that are absent or `INFRA_FAILED`/`FAILED` under `max_retries`. `RunStatus` (`records.py:32-42`) already separates infra vs eval failure, which is exactly the retry signal.

**3. Trigger.** Prefer a **poll-reconcile loop** over a push event bus (matches the codebase's existing 300s evaldash ingest and avoids new infra): list eligible checkpoints, join against existing records, launch the missing/retryable ones via `launch_group()`. Reconciliation is idempotent by construction, so "repeated events" is a non-issue. Open question for reviewers: run it as an Iris cron job, or fold into an existing daemon? (see #6503 "Trigger definition" — still TBD there.)

**4. State + inspectability.** No new database — the record store *is* the state. Trigger decisions are derivable from records + policy; add a small `record.json` field linking the source `checkpoint_id` (currently absent — records have no checkpoint ref) so eval results are traceable back to the checkpoint and evaldash can surface it. Retry = ignore the failed record and let reconcile re-launch; no hand-editing DB state.

**5. Canary.** A test that stages a synthetic eligible checkpoint, runs one reconcile pass, and asserts a terminal record lands at the deterministic path and is picked up by ingest — end to end, no manual `cli.py launch`.

Two decisions I need before implementing:
- **Trigger host**: Iris cron vs. extend evaldash ingest vs. a new daemon?
- **Eligibility source**: HF exports (`discover_hf_checkpoints`) vs. training `metadata.json` (`step`) — which is the canonical "checkpoint became available" signal for the first cut?

This is design-review work under #6503; I have not opened a PR.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Unify the HF release defaults and validation used by Levanter and vendored MarinSkyRL. The training backend should not silently determine the release precision, config field names, tokenizer metadata, or generation settings. Keep native training/recovery checkpoints separate from inference releases.

The published Snowball artifacts show the difference:

| Artifact | Tensor storage | Index total_size | Config |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [v0.1 at adc0078](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1/tree/adc0078a19a4383bc998fcdb43867b3360baf5f3) | 67,078,876,160 BF16 values; 6,656 FP32 values | 134,157,778,944 bytes | `dtype=bfloat16`; several names for the same architecture fields |
| [v0.1.1 at 59852d6](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1.1/tree/59852d6f07261722bbec1edb6ab148317156b58e) | 67,078,882,816 FP32 values | 268,315,531,264 bytes | `dtype=null`; canonical architecture field names |

Both indexes contain the same 502 tensor names, but use 39 and 79 shards respectively. The tokenizer.json and standalone chat_template.jinja file hashes match across these revisions. Both generation configs specify EOS IDs `[128001, 128009]` and BOS ID `128000`; the Transformers version annotation differs. v0.1.1 also embeds its chat template in tokenizer_config.json and adds `begin_suppress_tokens` to config.json. These are different trained models: this metadata comparison does not establish numerical equivalence or attribute output-quality differences to export. No weight payloads were downloaded for this investigation.

Code inspected at Marin `d9d49f2c65` shows export paths with different defaults:

- [Levanter's converter](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/hf_checkpoints.py#L488) preserves tensor dtype when `dtype=None`. An explicit dtype casts every floating tensor. Config construction is separate, so a weight cast alone does not establish matching dtype metadata. [The standalone export CLI](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/lib/levanter/src/levanter/main/export_lm_to_hf.py#L39) does not expose an export dtype; training hooks have a separate `hf_save_dtype` option. The published v0.1.1 export configuration does not specify a dtype.
- [SkyRL's Megatron export](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/distributed/megatron/megatron_strategy.py#L518) saves the materialized model through Bridge and then saves its HF config. Its Grug provider uses BF16 parameters and persistent FP32 router biases. [GrugMoeConfig](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/models/grug_moe.py#L310) stores duplicate aliases; Levanter already has a [single-name export contract](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py#L80). Do not adopt SkyRL's duplicate-field output as the common format.
- Generation and publication policies also differ. Levanter writes generation_config.json when explicitly supplied. [SkyRL](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/distributed/strategy.py#L125) tries to load it from the source model and continues after failure. SkyRL has tokenizer normalization and ordered manifest publication in [hf_model_io.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/hf_model_io.py); its export verification checks shard presence, not agreement between tensor headers and config semantics.

Use a small framework-neutral policy and validation layer that both exporters can import. Keep JAX conversion, distributed gathers, and Megatron Bridge conversion in their existing backends. Reuse the existing canonical-config, generation-config, tokenizer, and manifest helpers where appropriate; do not add a Levanter dependency on Marin or SkyRL. Persist the resolved policy in each export request so retries cannot change its meaning.

Done when:

- Public inference exports resolve one versioned policy: a BF16 release mode with architecture-declared FP32 exceptions, an FP32 mode, and a preserve-source-dtype mode. Architecture schemas declare required tensors and minimum precision; every mode must satisfy them. Preserve router biases and other required high-precision state. Do not apply a blanket BF16 cast or change native resume checkpoints. Invalid policies fail before export.
- Levanter standalone, training-hook and merged-adapter HF exports, plus SkyRL checkpoint-export jobs, use the same policy. Inventory additional supported entry points and migrate their callers in the same change; adapter-only PEFT artifacts retain their own format. Write canonical architecture fields once; reject conflicting aliases and unsupported conversions. Preserve behavior-critical fields, including context length, RoPE, attention layout, expert layout/schema, and effective router bias. Keep full Grug/Hero variants distinct from the narrower Snowball architecture.
- Tokenizer vocabulary, special-token IDs, chat templates, EOS lists, and generation controls have validated precedence: explicit export-request values, checkpoint metadata, pinned source-HF metadata, then documented defaults for optional fields. Reject missing behavior-critical values. Required metadata cannot disappear after a failed source lookup. Do not introduce suppression or stopping changes as a side effect of serialization.
- A shared validator checks actual safetensors names, shapes, dtypes, index coverage and byte totals against the declared policy and model schema. Record source checkpoint/step, source-model HF commit and checkpoint identity, exporter code revision, policy version, and file hashes. Publish a completion manifest only after weights and metadata validate; preserve current bounded-memory export and retry behavior.
- Tests export the same tiny Snowball/Grug model state through Levanter and the distributed Megatron export path and compare effective config, tensor layout/dtypes, tokenizer rendering, stop behavior, and logits within justified precision tolerances. Include nonzero FP32 router bias, explicit FP32 export, invalid aliases, missing metadata, interrupted publication, and retry. Before enabling the shared release defaults, load a representative Snowball export in the supported Marin vLLM runtime and verify fixed-prompt logits within declared tolerances plus termination on each configured EOS token. Keep existing published revisions immutable; assess any replacement release separately.

Related prior work: #7366 requested HF config/serialization standardization; #9039 tracks the separate Grug import round-trip gap; #7954 concerns chat-template consistency. This issue defines the shared export contract across trainers.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

Levanter’s HF writer preserves source dtype when `dtype` is omitted, and its config builder derives `begin_suppress_tokens` from tokenizer IDs. Marin’s pinned external MarinSkyRL revision writes Bridge weights and config separately, tolerates a failed source generation-config lookup, and lacks the former vendored `hf_model_io.py` validator/manifest helper. [PR #10112](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10112) changes the same Levanter export files; no open PR covers this shared release contract.

**Relevant code**
- [`hf_checkpoints.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/hf_checkpoints.py#L988-L1248) — dtype, config, shard upload
- [`snowball.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py#L75-L130) — canonical Snowball field names
- [`external_dependencies.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/external_dependencies.py#L70-L82) — pinned external SkyRL revision
- [`megatron_strategy.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/a906145aaf2bee56e3d8062830ef463f67722ea2/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/distributed/megatron/megatron_strategy.py#L317-L333) — Bridge weight conversion and config write
- [`strategy.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/a906145aaf2bee56e3d8062830ef463f67722ea2/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/distributed/strategy.py#L114-L141) — optional generation-config lookup

# Shared HF release contract

## Background

The two Snowball revisions in the issue demonstrate different release representations, but their training runs differ. The new contract must specify a release independently of the trainer and reject an export that cannot satisfy it. Native recovery checkpoints and existing published revisions remain separate artifacts.

## Design

1. Add a small `marin-hf-release` distribution under `lib/hf_release/`, importable by Levanter and MarinSkyRL without importing JAX, Torch, or Marin. A frozen, versioned `ExportRequest` records `schema_id`, precision mode (`bf16`, `fp32`, or `preserve`), source checkpoint URI/step/identity, pinned source-HF commit, resolved tokenizer and generation metadata, destination, and exporter revision. Resolve and validate it before loading or gathering weights; persist its canonical JSON and digest so a retry uses the same request. An unknown mode, unpinned source lookup, or missing required metadata fails before export.

2. Register separate Snowball and full Grug/Hero schemas. Each declares required tensor names/shapes, minimum dtype per tensor, canonical config keys, allowed aliases on input, and required architectural fields (context/RoPE, attention, experts, effective router bias). Normalize equal aliases to one canonical key and reject conflicting aliases or unsupported schema conversions. In `bf16`, cast eligible floating weights to BF16 but keep schema-declared FP32 state, including nonzero router bias; reject a source that has already lost required precision. In `fp32`, write all floating weights as FP32; in `preserve`, keep source dtypes if they satisfy the schema. Nonfloating state is never cast. Set config `dtype` to `bfloat16` or `float32` for the corresponding mode; preserve mode retains a single source dtype only when homogeneous, otherwise omits the scalar and records per-tensor dtypes in the manifest.

3. Resolve tokenizer vocabulary, IDs, chat template, EOS list, and generation controls field by field in this order: explicit request, checkpoint metadata, pinned source-HF metadata, documented optional defaults. Reject absent behavior-critical fields and disagreement between resolved tokenizer, config, and generation config. Preserve explicit stopping and suppression settings; do not synthesize `begin_suppress_tokens` from BOS/EOS/PAD. Validate the rendered template and all token IDs against the saved tokenizer.

4. Validate safetensors headers and index against the schema before publication: exact tensor coverage, names, shapes, dtypes, shard references, and `total_size` computed from tensor byte sizes. Hash each file while processing one shard at a time; put hashes, source identities, code revision, policy version, and request digest in a completion manifest. Upload weights and metadata first, verify destination objects using upload checksums and sizes, then publish the manifest last. A retry returns an already validated matching release, invalidates a partial completion marker, and refuses a different request digest at the same destination. Keep the current bounded-memory shard writer and Bridge collectives.

5. Route Levanter’s standalone CLI, LM/DPO hooks, merged LoRA export, `lora_lm`, ASR, and Marin’s `ConvertCheckpointStepConfig` through the resolved request at the common `HFCheckpointConverter.save_pretrained` boundary. Adapter-only PEFT saves keep their own format. Update MarinSkyRL’s `save_hf_model` and export-only job to use the same package and validator; release a pinned dependency, then update `config/external/MarinSkyRL/uv.lock` and regenerate Marin’s external dependency metadata. Coordinate Levanter changes with #10112. Do not change native checkpoint writers.

## Costs / risks

- The contract spans two repositories and an isolated SkyRL launcher. The shared distribution must be available to both runtimes before Marin advances its SkyRL pin.
- Hashing reads every completed shard once; validation should run beside the writer and avoid cross-region reads. Publication remains incomplete until the final manifest is visible.

## Testing and rollout

- Unit tests cover all three modes, a nonzero FP32 router bias, alias conflicts, missing metadata, EOS and chat-template precedence, bad index totals, missing/extra tensors, interrupted upload, and retry with the same versus different request digest.
- Export one identical tiny Snowball/Grug state through Levanter and a distributed Megatron Bridge job. Compare effective config, tensor names/shapes/dtypes, tokenizer rendering, stopping on each EOS ID, and logits with tolerances measured and declared for BF16 and FP32.
- Before making BF16 the default for public releases, load a representative staged Snowball artifact in the current pinned Marin vLLM runtime and check fixed-prompt logits and termination on every configured EOS token. Record the runtime revision, checkpoint identity, prompts, and tolerances with the gate result; publish a replacement only as a new revision.

## Open question

Which source checkpoint should serve as the representative promotion gate? The contract and local tests can land before that gate; the shared release default should wait for its result.

🤖 Research

The vendored SkyRL writer uses Megatron Bridge for weights, then saves config and tokenizer separately. Its `hf_model_io.py` checks that shards exist and publishes a manifest, but does not compare tensor headers with the config or a release precision policy. Levanter's shared converter preserves source dtype by default and can cast every floating tensor, including persistent FP32 router bias; its config builder also synthesizes `begin_suppress_tokens`. [Levanter writer](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/hf_checkpoints.py#L1081), [SkyRL Bridge writer](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/distributed/megatron/megatron_strategy.py#L518), [SkyRL publication helper](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/hf_model_io.py#L20).

Proposed Fix

Add a small framework-neutral release policy and safetensors validator in this repository. Resolve and persist the precision and metadata request before export; preserve schema-declared FP32 tensors, canonicalize Grug config fields, validate weights and metadata, and publish the completion manifest last. Wire Levanter's exporter callers and vendored SkyRL's checkpoint-export job to the shared contract. Keep BF16 release selection explicit until the representative vLLM gate specified in this issue passes. [PR #10480](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10480) changes native checkpoint schedules and FP32 master export, so this PR will leave those checkpoint paths intact.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Adjusted WSM-inspired checkpoint averaging → donor initialization of five chat-token output columns → 64 updates of LoRA plus vocabulary SFT produced a provisional Hero checkpoint for short RL capacity-planning trials. All 100 reviewed responses ended at EOT within the 2,048-token cap. Content errors and two special-token anomalies remain; intended-backend throughput and parity still need measurement.

The canonical research record has moved to [marin-logbooks #2](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/issues/2), following the workflow in [#9467](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9467). Its [commit-pinned notebook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/d152151d8148734c8f1a954be1224eb83e20c2e9/logbooks/2-hero-checkpoint-format-sft/notebook.md) preserves the full rationale, derivation, source revisions, commands, failed attempts and results. Future research updates belong there. This issue retains the checkpoint handoff and links to the selected Marin contribution.

## What we tried and why

The goal was basic coherent thinking and turn-taking for systems experiments without waiting for a separate full-model cooldown or full-model SFT. Hero is a roughly 535B MoE: 48 layers, hidden width 6,144, 384 routed experts with eight selected per token and two shared experts. This campaign retained its 16K architecture. A is the original pretraining checkpoint at step 294000.

1. **A → B, adjusted averaging.** Inspired by [Warmup-Stable and Merge (WSM)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.17634), divide the integrated target linear-cooldown LR by the integrated actual LR over each saved checkpoint interval. This gave weights 0.232123642 / 0.499105160 / 0.268771198 on steps 282000 / 288000 / 294000. Preserve the latest effective FP32 router bias. This is an offline approximation; no counterfactual optimizer trajectory was run.
2. **B → C, chat-token initialization.** Seed five output columns for header/thinking/EOT tokens from existing text/EOS donor tokens. Input embeddings initially stayed unchanged. Construction and ancestry were verified; no donor/no-donor ablation was run.
3. **C → D, compact SFT.** Freeze the base and routing control; train rank-16/alpha-16 [LoRA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685) on attention/shared dense projections plus five input/output vocabulary deltas. Use 4,806 no_robots training conversations, the shared Marin chat recipe and pinned tokenizer. Continue an eight-update smoke to 64 total with full Adam, counters and deterministic data position retained. Extending the LR horizon from 8 to 64 raised the first resumed LR from the short tail; it was not a schedule reset. Export ordinary BF16 weights with the deltas baked in.

## How we measured it

| Measurement | Result and scope |
| --- | --- |
| Matched A/B pretraining loss | Identical 59 C4 sequences of 16,384 tokens: 2.130703034 → 2.109083774 (−1.01465%); all 59 row deltas lower. One fixed panel, not broad-domain quality or cooldown equivalence. |
| Training-source EOT acquisition | Mean NLL for one expected EOT token at each of 16 fixed training prefixes: 3.38140 at update 8 → 0.42875 at 64; top-1 1/16 → 14/16. This is EOT-token NLL, not average sequence NLL or heldout evidence. |
| Fresh responses | 40 math, 40 Python and 20 fixed-history followups at temperature 0.7. All 100 stopped at EOT; zero caps; median 113.5 tokens, max 496. Math: 33 correct, four wrong, two incomplete, one ambiguous; code: 32 statically plausible, eight defects; history: 18 clear passes, one error, one borderline. Code was not executed. |

Training processed 67,108,864 positions, including 65,975,980 non-padding tokens: about 47.6 training-corpus token-volume equivalents. This reuse limits interpretation of acquisition gains. Capacity-overflow endpoints were 0.17389 at update 8 and 0.19403 at 64 on different batches; their quality impact is unassessed.

The [reviewed-output gist](https://gist.github.com/dlwh/408759a8eb09796d253b8b53a43769d4) retains every prompt, response and per-case judgment. Native sampling used dropless execution, full-prefix recomputation without KV cache and 4,096 physical padding. Its timing is not an RL-serving throughput measurement. Full heldout/native format/content evaluation, independent merge parity, post-SFT matched C4 regression, long-context behavior and backend agreement remain unresolved.

## Checkpoint artifacts


The merged step-64 native checkpoint contains the LoRA and vocabulary updates baked into ordinary BF16 weights. It needs no runtime adapter:

```text
s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-format-sft/2026.10.21/sft-phase-2416e9d7/SFT-long-test-v1-20261022/attempts/c77824dfce148a77/export/step-64
```

Canonical metadata digest: `aeec732ddaa4d47d146b0056b5b52891e5062a24a61857c35bb48f7e72cdfe57`.

The separate compact checkpoint retains adapters, five vocabulary deltas, full Adam state, counters and deterministic data position for training continuation:

```text
s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-format-sft/2026.10.21/sft-phase-2416e9d7/SFT-long-test-v1-20261022/attempts/c77824dfce148a77/adapters/step-64
```

Canonical metadata digest: `ce7a80fe9c7621e53d3f7745189a523473d7e228eb671a43039396924ae25fb6`.

Use `marin-community/marin-tokenizer` at revision `a5ca45f2feb6c959bd87b81689aa7279b5bdcaa2`, the shared MARIN chat template, and EOT token `128009`. Intended-backend loading and parity still need measurement.

## Status and contribution

[Marin #10556](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10556) retains the independently selected existing-interface fixes: activation-only short-convolution gradients for frozen weights, FP32 router-bias preservation during export and GB200 device typing. The [selection record](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/d152151d8148734c8f1a954be1224eb83e20c2e9/logbooks/2-hero-checkpoint-format-sft/selection.md) explains why the rest stays in the runnable research branch. The broad reproduction PR #10539 is superseded.

Next: load the merged checkpoint on the intended RL backend and measure throughput, latency and memory with representative lengths/concurrency and tokenizer/template/EOT checks. No further training, production adoption or merge is implied.

comments.author: davidlundgren
comments.body:
🤖 **Final results.** Training was stopped at step 10 (W&B `duu3twcu`).

| Step | AIME24 (avg@10) | SWE-bench Verified | Paired vs base (SWE-bench) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (base Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507) | 0.917 ± 0.007 | 0.046 (23/500) | — |
| 5 | 0.917 ± 0.008 | 0.070 (35/500) | +2.4 pts on 499 tasks (21 gained, 9 lost), p = 0.04 |
| 10 | 0.917 ± 0.007 | **0.156 (78/500)** | **+11.1 pts** on 496 tasks (59 gained, 4 lost), p < 0.001 |

The p-values come from an exact binomial test on the tasks whose outcome changed.

**Takeaways**
- SWE-bench Verified went from 4.6% to 15.6% (3.4×) in 10 steps.
- AIME24 did not move. In the Grug-SFT runs on the same recipe, AIME24 had already dropped from 0.83 to 0.80 by step 2–5.
- Much of the gain is likely format repair rather than new skill. The base model submits early, and about 2/3 of its trajectories hit at least one "No tool calls found" error.

**Training dynamics vs Grug (`lxm4qlxv`), same recipe**

| | Qwen start → step 10 | Grug start → step 10 |
|---|---|---|
| Held-out pivot accuracy | 0.175 → 0.374 | 0.285 → 0.390 |
| Train reward | 0.28 → 0.70 | 0.44 → 0.63 |
| Policy entropy | 0.565 → 0.389 | 0.448 → 0.157 |
| KL | 0 → 0.107 (sharp rise after step 8) | 0 → 0.011 |
| Tokens per response | ~1,000 → 546 (halved at step 9) | ~260 |

- Qwen's pass@16 held at about 0.92, while Grug's pass@8 fell from 0.89 to 0.70.

**Stopped at step 10:** step 11 hit a CUDA OOM in policy `ppo_train`. One actor was using 66.5 GB, plus 12.6 GB from a second process, likely the colocated reference model. Checkpoints exist for steps 5 and 10, with HF exports under `export/global_step_{5,10}/policy`.

**Eval infra notes**
- **AIME24 and preemption:** AIME24 (Evalchemy) needed about six resubmits because preemptions on cw-us-east-02a removed the inference endpoint (404), and Evalchemy has `max_task_failures=0`. Fixed by raising the outage grace to 40 min (iris22 workspace commit `c7118ec10b`).
- **Host memory on cw-rno2a:** with DP8, the 61 GB checkpoint OOMs a 256g host; it needs `--memory 768g`.
- **Cross-cluster export barrier:** the export-barrier job couldn't see a us-east export from rno2a. Worked around with a pre-verified export marker.
- **SWE-bench:** Harbor resumed cleanly across preemptions.

issues.author: rdolmedo
issues.body: Our aim is to predict the SWE-bench pass@1 of the final Snowball 9.97T base model after distilling on 2B tokens of SWE-smith trajectories generated by Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. We take the Snowball 3k, 9k, 18k, and 39k [intermediate checkpoints](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/snowball-intermediate) and [Grug](https://huggingface.co/penfever/grug-67b-a2b-sft-s1-wildchat-step257), and SFT them on [2B tokens](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nanoswe/swesmith-qwen3.6-35b-a3b) generated by a lightly fine-tuned variant of [Qwen3.6-35B-A3B](https://huggingface.co/nanoswe/qwen-3.6-35b-a3b-teacher) against the [SWE-smith](https://huggingface.co/datasets/SWE-bench/SWE-smith) problem set. We SFT the Snowball checkpoints at 0.21B and 0.64B token budgets, and Grug additionally at 0.37B, 1.1B, and 1.9B budgets. We evaluate the bpb of all fine-tunes on 1.3k SWE-smith trajectories generated by the teacher model. We also evaluate the pass@1 of the Grug fine-tunes. We fit two scaling laws, one relating pre-training steps and SFT budget to bpb, and a second relating bpb to pass@1. We obtain a final prediction of 33% pass@1 for the 9.97T Snowball checkpoint fine-tuned on our SFT dataset. ## Predicting bpb on teacher trajectories We use a multiplicative law. In ongoing work using pre-training checkpoints trained under constant LR (SmolLM3), we found the following law to work well: ```math \text{bpb} = E \left(1 + A\, D_{\text{pre}}^{-\alpha}\right) \left(1 + B\, D_{\text{sft}}^{-\beta}\right) ``` To account for the LR schedule of Snowball, we use the approach of [Scaling Law with Learning Rate Annealing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11029) to model both the Grug anneal and the Snowball anneal. We thus turn $`1 + A\, D_{\text{pre}}^{-\alpha}`$ into ```math 1 + A\, S_1^{-\alpha} - C\, S_2 ``` where $`S_1 = 10^{-4} \sum_i \eta_i / \eta_{\text{peak}}`$ is the LR area over pre-training optimizer steps (proportional to $`D_{\text{pre}}`$ at constant LR, warmup counted at peak), and $`S_2 = 10^{-3} \sum_i m_i`$ is the annealing area, with momentum $`m_i = \lambda\, m_{i-1} + (\eta_{i-1} - \eta_i) / \eta_{\text{peak}}`$, $`\lambda = 0.999`$ (as in Tissue et al.), and $`\eta_{\text{peak}} = 5.28 \times 10^{-3}`$. The full law is ```math \text{bpb} = E \left(1 + A\, S_1^{-\alpha} - C\, S_2\right) \left(1 + B\, D_{\text{sft}}^{-\beta}\right) ``` with $`D_{\text{sft}}`$ in billions of tokens. We fit the six coefficients on our 13 datapoints using least squares, obtaining $`E = 0.0538,\ A = 0.278,\ \alpha = 0.783,\ C = 0.124,\ B = 0.260,\ \beta = 0.306`$, and a df-adjusted RMSE of 0.000441 bpb. Extrapolating to 9.97T pre-training tokens at 1.93B SFT tokens, we predict 0.0635 bpb. It is unclear whether calibrating the law on the much shorter Grug cooldown will extrapolate to the cooldown of Snowball. ## From bpb to pass@1 We fit the following law: ```math \log \text{pass@1} = a - b \cdot \text{bpb} ``` We fit the law using OLS on the five Grug SFTs, obtaining $`a = 5.98`$ and $`b = 39.1`$ (i.e., $`\text{pass@1} = 397\, e^{-39.1 \cdot \text{bpb}}`$), and extrapolate to the bpb predicted by the previous law, resulting in a predicted pass@1 of 33%. The 95% CI on the mean at the forecast is large: 29.3% to 37.5% pass@1. Our hunch is that the 33% prediction might be slightly conservative: fitting the law on only the three largest SFT budgets instead predicts 35%. ## Conclusion Our laws predict that fine-tuning the final Snowball checkpoint on our 2B Qwen3.6-35B-A3B dataset will result in a SWE-bench pass@1 of **33%**. If anything we expect to err low, and would not be surprised by 35%.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body: Nice work @RicardoDominguez !

comments.author: rdolmedo
comments.body:
**Update (Lightning SFT data).** We now fine-tune on SWE-smith trajectories generated by Nemotron 3.5 Lightning instead of Qwen 3.6. This is a separate prediction from the 33% above, which used Qwen 3.6 data and a different eval harness. We pre-register a new prediction for the final Snowball base model, as released by Marin, fine-tuned on **7.55B Lightning tokens** with the recipe of our Grug Lightning ladder (3,600 steps, 32k context). We evaluate on SWE-bench Verified (483 instances, 5 attempts each).

![Snowball Lightning forecast](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/rdolmedo/2ad458a02acae99b551f3739fa16834c/raw/e68176824598a2884c5b4fa02689f56094e3f0ac/forecast.png)

**Loss.** We predict **0.1334 bpb** on held-out Lightning trajectories. We start from Grug's measured Lightning loss at the same budget and subtract the Snowball–Grug gap predicted by the law above. To convert that gap from Qwen 3.6 loss to Lightning loss, we use the teacher map fitted at matched budgets on four students (SmolLM3 base, SmolLM3 mid-trained, Qwen3-4B, Grug):

```math
L_{\text{Lightning}} = 1.711\, L_{\text{Qwen 3.6}} + 0.033
```

We apply only its slope to the gap: $`\Delta L_{\text{Lightning}} = 1.711\, \Delta L_{\text{Qwen 3.6}}`$.

**pass@1.** We use three links. Each maps loss $`L`$ to ability $`\theta`$, and $`\theta`$ to pass@1 through a Rasch model averaged over the 483 instances, $`\text{pass@1} = \frac{1}{483}\sum_i \sigma(\theta - z_i)`$. Link 1 uses the instance difficulties $`z_i`$ fitted on the 29-model sweep; links 2 and 3 share difficulties fitted on the 25 Lightning fine-tunes.

| Link | $`\theta(L)`$ | pass@1 |
|---|---|---|
| Global ability law | $`13.22 - 47.59\,L`$ | **41.6%** |
| One law across four students on Lightning (SmolLM3 base/mid, Qwen3-4B, Grug) | $`10.94 - 68.17\,(1 - r\,e^{-D/D_0})\,L`$, with Grug's $`r = 0.065`$, $`D_0 = 4.57\text{B}`$ | **40.3%** |
| Grug only (linear) | $`8.39 - 48.98\,L`$ | **39.4%** |

We expect the law across four students to be the most accurate, which gives a final predicted pass@1 of **40.3%**.

We also pre-register each link as a function of the measured loss (middle panel), so the links can be checked even if the loss prediction misses.

All three have now completed. Refitting on the complete evals changes links 2 and 3 slightly. Link 1 does not use these fine-tunes, so it is unchanged. At the predicted loss of 0.1334 bpb:

comments.author: rdolmedo
comments.body:
**Update (released base).** Our predictions assumed the end of the final 65K cooldown (step 156,000, 9.97T tokens). The base model Marin released is [`open-athena/snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175-skew8`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175-skew8) (step 157,000; #7495). It is the same run after 1,000 more steps (67B tokens) of 262K-context extension, during which the learning rate decays from 5% to 1% of peak (#8813).

**Loss.** Under our law, the extra annealing raises $`S_2`$ from 0.6496 to 0.6687 ($`S_1`$: 8.239 → 8.242), which lowers Snowball's predicted loss by 0.25%. Mapped to Lightning as before, the predicted loss goes from 0.1334 to **0.1331 bpb**.

**pass@1.** With the links from our previous comment:

| Link | pass@1 |
|---|---|
| Global ability law | **41.8%** (previously 41.6%) |
| One law across four students on Lightning | **40.6%** (previously 40.4%) |
| Grug only (linear) | **39.7%** (previously 39.6%) |

Our final predicted pass@1 is **40.6%**.

comments.author: rdolmedo
comments.body: **Resolved** **1. End-to-end prediction** Measured pass@1: **38.4%**. Missed by +1.3 pp (+3.3%) to +3.4 pp (+8.9%). | 7.55B | bpb | pass@1, law 1 (global) | pass@1, law 2 (four students, primary) | pass@1, law 3 (Grug only) | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Pre-registered** | 0.1331 | 41.8% | **40.6%** [95% CI 39.6, 41.4] | 39.7% | | **Measured** | 0.1380 | 38.4% ± 1.1 | 38.4% ± 1.1 | 38.4% ± 1.1 | | **Miss** | −0.0048 (−3.5%) | +3.4 pp (+8.9%) | **+2.2 pp (+5.6%)** | +1.3 pp (+3.3%) | **2. bpb -> pass@1 link** Most of the error in the end-to-end prediction lies in the bpb prediction rather than the bpb to pass@1 link. Evaluated at the measured bpb, the errors shrink to −0.8 pp (−2.0%) to +0.1 pp (+0.2%). | 7.55B | bpb (input) | pass@1, law 1 (global) | pass@1, law 2 (four students, primary) | pass@1, law 3 (Grug only) | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Link prediction at the measured bpb** | 0.1380 | 38.5% | 37.8% | 37.6% | | **Link miss** | — | +0.1 pp (+0.2%) | −0.6 pp (−1.5%) | −0.8 pp (−2.0%) | This gives me optimism, since I thought the pass@1 link would be the more problematic component. With a proper scaling ladder (rather than intermediate checkpoints of a run with an LR schedule and long-context extension), we should be able to predict bpb more accurately. **3. Post-training scaling** We were not able to accurately predict the SFT scaling behavior. The low-SFT points did much better than predicted with the $r$ and $D_0$ fitted on Grug. The result is consistent with our paper's thesis that pre-training raises performance at low SFT budgets, but performance eventually converges to the shared bpb->pass@1 line. This means predicting performance at low SFT budgets is still an open problem, whereas the more we SFT, the easier downstream performance is to predict.

comments.author: mcwitt-agent
comments.body:
🤖 Storage incident on 2026-09-23/24, now resolved. At 23:44Z the US-EAST-08A CoreWeave account reached 104.56 TiB against its 100 TiB quota, and CoreWeave suspended writes (`405 MethodNotAllowed: Account is write suspended for this availability zone`). Most of the 11.7 TiB rise since 20:26Z came from this deploy's forced checkpoints and durable handoff copies in `hero-checkpoints`.

- The step-146585 save staged at 23:43:47Z and hung: rank 0 blocked in the s3fs manifest upload, which has no timeout. Training and logs stopped with no error. The step watchdog restarted the gang at about 00:00Z (attempt 1), which restored `step-146355`.
- Russell's cleanup brought usage to about 80 TB by 00:21Z. Writes were accepted again from 00:39Z.
- Attempt 1's step-146582 save at 01:01Z then stalled. 448 of 704 processes finished their upload; the other 256, spread over 132 hosts, stopped writing at 01:01:55Z with no error, and the commit never completed. Host memory stayed about 260 GiB below the limit. The cause is not confirmed; a storage-side stall left over from the suspension is the leading explanation. Training continued because checkpoint uploads run in background threads, but the next save would have blocked on it, so the task was preempted at 01:40Z (attempt 2, again from `step-146355`).
- Since then, saves `step-146582` (02:43Z) and `step-146817` (03:44Z) committed normally, and the first evaluation at step 147000 matched the trend: dropless loss 1.9086 against 1.9098 at step 144000.
- Cost: steps 146355–146732 were trained twice, plus about two hours of hangs and restarts.
- Cleanup: about 49 TB of stale temporary checkpoints and duplicates were deleted from `hero-checkpoints`. The durable handoff copies for steps 108778, 121638, and 146139 remain. The step-81716 handoff was deleted during the incident cleanup, and no durable copy of the step-58014 handoff was found.

The run has lost at least 78 minutes since the failed save and would replay steps 197638–197999 from the selected checkpoint. Next: have a node-read-authorized operator verify `s2brxs64` boot/health and storage connectivity, escalate the 400/502 evidence to CoreWeave storage support, then have the production owner decide on targeted recovery. issues.author: davidlundgren
issues.body:
🤖

Every RL turn passes through [`DirectModelClient._generate_chat`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3ae74d9560/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/trajectory_runners/model_clients.py#L296-L301). That method already decodes the exact response tokens with special tokens kept, then calls `final_answer_text`. `<|start_think|>` and `<|end_think|>` are single special tokens, so a check on the decoded text sees the same span boundaries as a check on token IDs. The fix changes only vendored SkyRL code. `rolloutengine` and `ModelTurn` stay the same.

1. In `answer_extraction.py`, add `reasoning_span_violation(text) -> ReasoningViolation | None`. `ReasoningViolation` is a `StrEnum` with the values `UNCLOSED`, `SECOND_SPAN`, and `STRAY_END`. When the text has a violation, `final_answer_text` returns `""`, so `<|start_think|>A<|end_think|>B<|end_think|>C` no longer grades as `C`.
2. In `_generate_chat`, when the response has a violation, clear `tool_calls` and `content` so that no tool call runs, and record the violation in the turn's `metadata`. The sampled tokens and log probabilities stay the same.
3. In `task_worker.py`, if any turn of a rollout has a violation, grade it as `Outcome.SUBMISSION_FAILURE` with reward 0. This also covers a SWE rollout that fixed the repo in earlier turns and then produced a malformed turn.
4. Tests: one parser case for each violation, one transport case that shows the tool call is dropped, and one rollout whose earlier turn is malformed but whose final answer is correct (expected reward 0).

These parts of the done-when list are deferred:
- the missing-span and `/nothink`-span checks, which depend on #10519
- the Baby RSI transport, on #9626
- the thinking-enabled probe, on #10399

`has_reasoning_format_violation` stays unchanged. It reproduces NVIDIA's penalty for plain-text `<think>` tags, and step 1 covers the special-token markers.

comments.author: davidlundgren
comments.body: 🤖 #10542 implements the revised plan. Rollouts with an unclosed span, a second span, or a stray end marker in any turn now get reward 0, and the malformed turn's tool calls don't run. Still open: the missing-span and `/nothink` checks (#10519), pinned-prompt requests (decoded without special tokens), Baby RSI (#9626), and the probe (#10399).

comments.author: davidlundgren
comments.body:
🤖 Baseline for #10542: malformed reasoning spans during plain RLVR from the 10.05 SFT.

The source is #10214 arm A at seed 42 (RLVR1 only, started from `Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05`). I scanned the training trajectories it retained (`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/dml/skyrl/pivot-mixed-rlvr/runs/pivot-mixed-rlvr-a-20261018-001718/attempts/trajectories`). Retention kept close to every rollout: 3,000–8,700 per step, against 512 prompts × 16 samples. Each sampled turn is checked on its token IDs with the rules in #10542. A turn that stopped on the length limit inside its span counts as truncation, so it isn't included.

| 12 | 5,340 | 542 | 10.2% | 30 | 0.056 | 0.250 | 61 / 187 / 294 |

The malformed rate rises from 2.3–3.2% in steps 1–3 to 10.2% at step 12. In steps 1–3 a malformed rollout earns less than half the reward of a well-formed one. In steps 4–10 it earns about the same or more (step 9 excepted), so during that stretch RL does not push back on the habit. The form shifts from stray end markers (steps 3–6) to second spans and unclosed spans (steps 8–12), which matches the stacked blocks seen in Smartie. Most malformed rollouts are in single-step tool use (1,155 of 27,538) and instruction following (801 of 10,086); NVARC transductive has the highest rate (364 of 3,335). `genrm_simple_agent_reasoning_off` has 29 malformed rollouts out of 388, and the `/nothink` check that waits on #10519 would reject more of them.

The scan uses one seed. Rollouts per step vary by a factor of almost 3, so single steps are noisy.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
On TPU, Snowball Step12 assigns different next-token log probabilities than H100 from token position 2048 onward. Up to position 2047 the two platforms agree to within TPU run-to-run noise. Step12 uses `sliding_window = 2048` with `global_every = 4`, so three of every four attention layers attend only to the last 2048 tokens. The divergence starts at that window size.

Impact: MATH500 on the same model, revision and Evalchemy commit scores 0.944 and 0.950 on H100 and 0.878, 0.882 (v6e-8, TP8) and 0.884 (v5p-8, TP4) on TPU. 39 items are correct on both H100 runs and wrong on TPU; 22 of them are long answers that drift to a different question.

Measurement: teacher-forced log probabilities of the same 10 texts on each platform (rendered Step12 chat prefix plus an H100-generated, H100-correct MATH500 completion; vLLM `/v1/completions` with `echo`, `logprobs=1`, `max_tokens=0`, concurrency 1). 35,801 scored positions; token ids are identical on both platforms.

| Positions | H100 vs TPU mean \|Δlogprob\| | top-1 token differs | TPU concurrency 1 vs 10 mean \|Δlogprob\| |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–2047 | 0.010–0.019 | 0.8–1.0% | 0.012–0.015 |
| 2048–2111 | 0.026 | 1.6% | – |
| 2368–2559 | 0.066 | 3.1–3.3% | – |
| 2048–3071 | 0.063 | 3.6% | 0.014 |
| 3072–4095 | 0.142 | 6.8% | 0.018 |

Pooled over all positions: mean \|Δ\| 0.056 (TPU self-noise 0.014), maximum 12.3 (TPU self-noise 1.1), top-1 differs at 2.8% of positions (TPU self-noise 0.86%). TPU's mean per-token negative log likelihood is higher on all 10 items.

The per-element window mask agrees across the three stacks. Each keeps the last W tokens including the query token:
- training: [`levanter/grug/attention/_core.py` L126](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8e99858a17df0463daac6b104f5eddb0ffa79ffd/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_core.py#L123-L126), `k >= q - (W - 1)`;
- H100 vLLM fork: [`grugmoe.py` L957-L964](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/01911be34fac8715347962a8d791ca34a879e01e/vllm/model_executor/models/grugmoe.py#L957-L964) passes `per_layer_sliding_window=2048` on local layers;
- TPU: [`grugmoe.py` L786](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/models/jax/grugmoe.py#L776-L787) passes the window as `attention_chunk_size`, which [`attention_interface.py` L496](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/layers/common/attention_interface.py#L494-L498) forwards as `sliding_window`; the RPA v3 kernel masks with [`q < k + W` at L494](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L493-L494).

The cause is not confirmed. Two unverified suspects on the TPU path:
- the RPA v3 sliding-window block skipping, which computes the first KV block to read from `kv_q_gap - sliding_window` ([kernel.py L388-L399](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L388-L399), [L916-L942](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L916-L942));
- KV-cache handling for the sliding-window layers.

Reproduce:
1. Serve `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02` at revision `50fe2f488aee7730bbccc721024b35229075602e`, bf16. TPU: v6e-8, TP8, tpu-inference `ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d`, vLLM `fb02daf1d7139d2adaeb0588448649591657d1e3`. H100: H100x8, DP8 with expert parallelism, Marin vLLM fork build `01911be34fac`.
2. Run `python teacher_forced_logprobs.py --endpoint URL --model open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02 --items teacher_forced_items.json --output DIR --concurrency 1` against each server. The client and items (sha256 `9d4779361b79259d36dcd2402d6fe686c81884d111cab550bb6c7fff158cdc4d`) are in `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task236/inputs/`.
3. Compare with `python compare_tf.py H100_DIR/results.json TPU_DIR/results.json` from the same folder, and bin `|Δlogprob|` by position.

Expected: TPU per-position log probabilities stay within TPU run-to-run noise of H100 at every position, including beyond 2048.

Next step: rerun the TPU side with `grugmoe_attention_mode` set to the dense reference path (`_dense_reference_attention` in `grugmoe.py`, which applies the window as an explicit mask). If dense-mode TPU matches H100 past position 2048, the defect is in the production RPA path.

Caveats: the H100 completions were re-tokenized from text because the eval record has no sampled token ids, and vLLM omits special tokens such as the leading `<|start_think|>` from returned text. Both platforms scored the same bytes, so the comparison is valid, but the first completion positions are not a replay of the original sampled trajectory.

Data:
- H100: `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task236/teacher-h100x8/concurrency-1/`
- TPU v6e-8: `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task236/teacher-v6e8/concurrency-{1,10}/`
- H100 MATH500 per-item and three-way tables: `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task224-math500/`

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

The 2048-token onset implicates local attention, but matching elementwise mask inequalities do not establish that TPU RPA visits the right KV blocks or reads intact cache pages. `GrugMoeAttention.__call__()` selects a dense path that computes from the full input without updating KV cache, or a production path that calls RPA v3. The measured TPU revision is the head of [tpu-inference#27](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/pull/27); [marin#9400](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9400) qualifies a June checkpoint, not Step12.

**Relevant code**
- [`grugmoe.py#L738-L805`](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/models/jax/grugmoe.py#L738-L805) — dense and production attention paths
- [`attention_interface.py#L493-L510`](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/layers/common/attention_interface.py#L493-L510) — window forwarded to RPA
- [`kernel.py#L388-L399`](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L388-L399) — first KV block selection
- [`kernel.py#L493-L494`](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L493-L494) — elementwise window mask
- [`kernel.py#L916-L942`](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L916-L942) — per-query-block traversal

# Proposed Fix

`GrugMoeAttention.__call__()` → `shared_attention()` → RPA v3 is the production call chain. The failing step within that chain is not established, so use the frozen Step12 inputs to isolate it:

1. Replay the issue's 10 teacher-forced inputs on the reported TPU revisions with `grugmoe_attention_mode=dense` and `production`; force one complete prefill per request because dense has no historical KV-cache reads, verify identical token IDs, and compare bins around position 2048 with the existing H100 results.
2. If dense agrees with H100, compare RPA v3 with a dense QKV reference at positions 2047, 2048, 2111, and 3072 across page and query-block boundaries, including full prefill, chunked prefill, decode, skipped KV blocks, and cache/page-table contents; otherwise find the first divergent layer output and compare its Q/K/V, RoPE, mask, and loaded weights with Levanter.
3. Fix the identified TPU fork path, add a regression across position 2048, rerun the frozen log-probability comparison and repeated MATH500 on the same checkpoint, and coordinate with the open `tpu-inference#27` stack before updating Marin's paired fork pin; the post-window H100–TPU error should return to measured TPU run-to-run noise before hardware qualification.
